Esri World Imagery (summer) 240 m frames around 39.7424,-92.0400 and 39.7473,-92.0350, viewed 2026-11-09
note: Wooded tract on the North Fork Salt River north of Shelbina. Two primitive camping spots: at the river fishing-access lot at the end of a short gravel road off Highway 15 (this pin), and at a small gravel pull-off on Shelby 336 along the north boundary, 665 m away. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: two MDC primitive camping areas (map + GIS), free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit. They are 665 m apart on separate roads - under the 1 km split line, so one entry; pin kept on the main river-access lot. Not waterfront confirmed (creek-sized river ~25-30 m from the lot through trees).
flags: INCLUSION/FIT: the area page lists 'Designated Camping Sites' (and walk/float/backpack open camping); the 04/14 area map marks two 'Primitive Camping Area' symbols, matched by two GIS camping points. (1) SW, the stored pin 39.74248,-92.03987: a gravel lot (~25 x 20 m) at the end of a ~250 m gravel access road from Highway 15 beside the river, camping point 26 m from the lot - a 23-ft rig reaches it, no ford. (2) NE 39.7473,-92.03527: a tiny gravel pull-off (~10 m) on the south side of gravel Shelby 336, camping point under canopy 60 m west of it - tight for a 23-ft rig. MDC's lot records say Allows_Trailers 'No' at both.
NO SPLIT: the two areas are 665 m apart with separate roads (Hwy 15 access road vs Shelby 336) - under the ~1 km line; pin kept on the SW river-access lot, the larger of the two.

WATERFRONT (stored not waterfront): confirmed. The North Fork Salt River (~20 m wide, creek-sized) runs ~25-30 m SE of the SW lot behind a wooded strip with a gravel bar beyond; no open apron, view under canopy not confirmable. The NE spot is ~400 m from the river.
Note rewritten: generic MDC text and directions dropped; the two-spot layout described.
